content: On the two rounds where RoBERTa was used as the base model, its performance is not much better than the hypothesis-only model. This could mean two things: either the test data is very difficult, or the training data is not good. To rule out the latter, we trained only on ANLI ($\sim $163k training examples): doing so with RoBERTa matches the performance of BERT on MNLI when it is trained on the much larger, fully in-domain SNLI+MNLI combined dataset (943k training examples), with both getting $\sim $86, which is impressive. Hence, this shows that our new challenge test sets are so difficult that the current state-of-the-art model cannot do better than a hypothesis-only prior.
